Body: Would be great to have that back.

Confirming this is still happening on 1.18.3 with OpenCode Zen/Go
I ran into the exact same pattern described in this issue, on a clean environment:

OpenCode version: 1.18.3
Provider: OpenCode Zen / OpenCode Go
Plugins: none (removed all plugins/custom agents to rule them out)
Environment: reproduced both inside VSCode/Antigravity integrated terminal and in a native Windows CMD terminal — same behavior in both, so it's not terminal-related

Steps to reproduce:

Run opencode in a project folder with no AGENTS.md, no plugins, default PLAN/BUILD agents only
Run /init to generate AGENTS.md
Agent completes the file, then ends its turn with a text-only follow-up question ("The task is complete. What would you like to do next?")
Instead of stopping and waiting for user input, the session immediately restarts and re-runs the same /init prompt from scratch, in an endless cycle

This matches the root cause already identified in this thread — a text-only response with finish_reason=stop and no tool calls isn't being treated as "stop and wait for user," so the session processor calls the LLM again automatically.

Provider is the deciding factor: the loop only happens with Zen/Go. **Switching the provider** to the official DeepSeek provider — same project, same /init task, nothing else changed — resolved it completely: the task completed cleanly, ended its turn, and waited for input as expected, with no restart. So this looks isolated to how Zen/Go's streaming responses are parsed, not a general OpenCode session bug. 

**With every other provider I've used, this issue simply does not occur.**

Again, a **10 second** difference in timeout period for a subagent, rolls over to an hour. Painful in the extreme. Enough to drop OpenCode for Pi altogether. Ridiculous UX deficiency. I saw it happening and have attached the screenshots to illustrate the anguish of every user affected by this. (Yes, I know it also looks overall 1h offset with the reported time, this is just z.ai things)

Confirming this is still happening (Jul 19, 2026), same signature, on `opencode` CLI **v1.17.3** (Linux).

Reproduced independently with a real, active OpenCode Go subscription key (usage well within weekly/monthly limits, balance-fallback enabled):

```
$ curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer <real-key>" https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models
HTTP/2 500
cf-ray: a1d77f53f905b4c9-MIA
server: cloudflare
content-type: application/json;charset=UTF-8

{"status":500,"unhandled":true,"message":"HTTPError"}
```

Same for `POST /chat/completions` with a valid model id (`deepseek-v4-flash`):
```
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"error","message":"Internal server error"}}
```

Consistent across multiple retries (not intermittent), and reproducible with **no auth header at all** or with an **obviously invalid key** — both also return the same generic 500, which suggests the failure happens before/regardless of auth resolution (not a per-account issue).

For comparison, the equivalent request against `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/...` (OpenCode **Zen**, not Go) on the same account returns a proper, specific error instead of a generic 500 (e.g. a `CreditsError` for that separate wallet), so whatever is throwing the unhandled exception seems specific to the `zen/go` route handler.

This is currently blocking all OpenCode Go models for us (TUI shows "Internal server error [retrying in 25s attempt #5]" and eventually gives up). Happy to provide more debug info if useful.

I'd like to take this one.

The generic piece is already in place — `discoverModels` on the provider custom-loader in `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts` — but only GitLab implements it and the call site is hardcoded to the `gitlab` provider, so Ollama / LM Studio / vLLM / llama.cpp never get their models discovered.

My change follows @rekram1-node's review on #8359:

- Add a `discoverModels` for OpenAI-compatible providers that GETs `{baseURL}/models` (baseURL from `options.endpoint ?? options.baseURL`).
- No new config option — models are sourced from the endpoint. Discovered ids are added only when not already known, so models.dev/config metadata still wins.
- Parallel across providers with a ~2s timeout, so a slow or unreachable endpoint can't block startup.
- Generalize the gitlab-only discovery loop to run every registered `discoverModels`.

Working locally with a test `/v1/models` server + tests. Any objection to the approach, or a preference for keeping this in `provider.ts` vs the newer `packages/llm` layer? I'll open the PR once you're good with it.

Confirmed a closely matching failure on macOS, suggesting this is not limited to the Linux/inotify backend.

Environment:

- macOS 26.2 (25C56), arm64
- OpenCode 1.18.2 (Homebrew)
- `opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 8088`
- User-level launchd supervisor, several existing projects in the global database

Observed behavior:

- The process remains alive and `LISTEN`ing on the port.
- Both `/` and `/global/health` accept the TCP connection but then return no bytes until the client timeout (5-8 seconds).
- Restarting the process restores HTTP immediately, but reconnecting web clients/workspaces eventually wedges it again.
- In an isolated test with several Web/SSE client tabs, a fresh process was healthy, then stopped answering HTTP about 70 seconds later.
- The supervisor recorded three consecutive failed HTTP probes before restarting the still-alive process.

Relevant log pattern before the hang:

```text
watcher backend directory=<project> platform=darwin backend=fs-events
project copy refresh started projectID=<id>
project copy refresh done projectID=<id> updated=[] removed=[]
booting location services directory=<project> workspaceID=undefined
```

After that, the server goes silent until it is killed. A forced restart can leave an `EINTR: interrupted system call, lstat '<project>'` entry from the interrupted bootstrap.

External plugins do not appear necessary for reproduction: the same HTTP wedge occurred with `opencode web --pure`. I also saw the Effect runtime `MaxListenersExceededWarning` signature reported in #28492/#29204, so there may be a second listener/SSE amplification path, but disabling plugins did not prevent the hard HTTP wedge.

I have now applied the workaround from this issue to the Web daemon:

```sh
export OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_FILEWATCHER=1
opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 8088
```

The normal plugin configuration is enabled again and HTTP health is restored. This is early validation; I am setting up a daily upstream/status check and will report back if the macOS `fs-events` backend still wedges with the watcher disabled.

This looks consistent with the same main-thread/native watcher startup deadlock occurring through `@parcel/watcher`'s macOS `fs-events` backend during multi-project attach.

Re: the bot's note about #34188 — I found that PR (and the now-closed #31121) after opening this one, so a quick note on how this differs, for whoever triages:

Both detect the legacy `(id, hash, created_at)` journal the same way. The difference is the seeding fallback:

- #34188 seeds by row count: `input.slice(0, count)` marks the first N TypeScript migrations completed, assuming the journal rows correspond 1:1 to the first N migrations in order. Nothing validates that assumption; if it doesn't hold the wrong migrations get marked completed silently.
- This PR maps each row's `created_at` back to the timestamp prefix of a known migration id — the same value the `effect-drizzle-sqlite` v0 -> v1 journal upgrader matches on (drizzle-kit derives the filename prefix from the timestamp it stores in `created_at`). Rows that don't map to any known migration abort with a descriptive error instead of seeding anything.

Verified against a real affected database (6 legacy journal rows, empty hashes): all rows mapped to the correct ids and the remaining migrations applied cleanly on top. This PR also keeps the diff to the migration path only.

Happy to defer to whichever approach the maintainers prefer — mostly want #31119 fixed, since affected installs currently freeze on startup with no visible error.
